paragraphs.source_en: Among the Round Head zoomorphic figures there is a special kind of animal not examined by previous scholars because its importance and singularity have not been recognised. Although the Round Head paintings are not very realistic it is nevertheless usually possible to identify the animal species from their special distinguishing marks such as hornsparallel and backwards for antelope, divergent to both sides for mouflon, tusks for warthogs, "butterfly" ears for elephants (Fig. 5-21), long neck for giraffes etc. These conventional marks used to determine the species were known to all the painters producing this art as is evident by their homogeneity all over the area.

paragraphs.source_en: There are however some animals which are not determinable. They may bear marks of more animals or, more often, they may have no marks as they consist only of a body with four limbs, a tail but no ears or horns. These unrecognisable animals, if ever taken in consideration, have been interpreted as various animal species. The subjectivity of such interpretations is best evident in the case of the Tin Aboteka animal (see figure 5-2) interpreted as a rhinoceros or bush pig by Tschudi (1955), as a feline by Lhote (1958) and as a bovid by Soleilhavoup (2007).

paragraphs.source_en: Since other animals are always recognisable when they possess their distinguishing marks, I argue that the form of the indeterminable quadrupeds is fully intentional and their particular form represents a special kind of animal. This hypothesis is further supported by the fact that only these indeterminable animals are always represented with their head downwards. It is their characteristic position which distinguishes them neatly from the recognisable animals which are never represented downheaded. What kind of behaviour may the down-headed position indicate? It does not seem to represent drinking or browsing since the head is never completely on the floor but only near to it. It rather evokes a position of submission or difficulty and, given this posture is repeated in all localities, it was certainly a significant piece of information to communicate.
